subject: Deployment-mode follow-up & hosted eval ops checklist
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Alexa Barnes <alexa@finosolutions.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment-mode follow-up & hosted eval ops checklist

Hi Alexa — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Appreciate the honest questions from your ML infra and product teams. Quick recap and a few operational questions so we can tailor the Hosted eval and confirm whether Hosted or Dedicated (or Private) is the best fit for Fino.

Summary of what we demoed:
- Redwood Hosted API: instant onboarding, REST/SDK endpoints for generation and embeddings, streaming, and rich telemetry in the Console.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools when you need predictable p99 throughputs and strict data isolation.
- Private/VPC: customer-managed network and optional on-prem for regulated flows.

Operational questions to help qualify:
1) Expected concurrent request pattern (peak qps and average): do you have an estimate for concurrent users and peak qps?
2) Typical prompt sizes and response length: average input tokens and expected reply tokens.
3) Data residency / retention constraints: is any PII required to be kept on-prem or excluded from hosted logs?
4) Rate-limit tolerance: is a slight throttling (short 429 backoffs) acceptable during spikes, or do you need guaranteed hard limits?
5) Timeline & success criteria for the eval: e.g., cost per request target, latency SLO (p95/p99), and functional benchmarks.

Quick next steps we suggest for a Hosted eval (we can tailor if you prefer Dedicated):
- We spin up a Hosted evaluation tenant for you (no infra commitment) — includes 2 models pre-baked and a test API key.
- Recommended traffic profile for the eval: 50 concurrent connections, average 30 req/s, sample requests attached (rate_limits_table.csv).
- Quickstart guide attached (redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf) with example curl/SDK calls and a checklist for KV caching and prompt templates.
- If you hit sustained higher QPS or require predictable tail latency, we can propose a Dedicated capacity estimate after we see initial traffic patterns.

Can you reply with the answers to 1–5 above? If helpful I can propose two time slots (Mon/Tue next week) for a short technical sync with your infra lead to validate the traffic profile.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0178

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf (guide), rate_limits_table.csv (sample traffic), sow-template.docx (for reference)
From: Alexa Barnes <alexa@finosolutions.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Deployment-mode follow-up & hosted eval ops checklist

Laura — thanks for the recap and the docs. Sorry for the short reply; I wanted to get answers back to you quickly so you can scope next steps. Answers inline below.

1) Concurrency / qps: Our first pilot will be internal-facing (24 power users) but we expect traffic to scale. For the pilot target: peak 70 qps, typical 15–20 qps.
2) Prompt / response sizes: prompts are around 150–300 tokens; responses average ~250 tokens (longer for summarization).
3) Data residency: Customer PII must be redacted for external storage; for the pilot we can use pseudonymized data. We prefer metadata logs to be retained for 30 days.
4) Rate limits tolerance: For pilot, short throttling/backoff is acceptable. Production will need a more predictable plan — would love to see Dedicated options if cost is within reason.
5) Timeline & criteria: Pilot start in Jan (2–4 week eval), success = p95 latency < 600ms for generation, cost target <$0.02 per successful request for our weighted workload.

Two asks: can you confirm the Hosted tenant will have streaming enabled and KV caching available? Also please share any recommended prompt engineering patterns for short latency (I glanced at the quickstart but the team would like a one-page checklist).

Best,
Alexa Barnes
Head of Product — Fino Solutions
Alexa@finosolutions.com

Thanks Alexa — helpful details. A couple notes from infra/solutions:
- Hosted tenant will have streaming enabled by default; KV prefix caching is available. We'll expose cache-control headers and a sample cache policy in the tenant.
- For the pilot profile (70 qps peak, 250-token responses), we expect Hosted to work fine for the eval but expect costs to scale linearly; if you need tighter p99 tail latency guarantees we should size a Dedicated pool.
- Suggested quick prompt checklist (short): 1) use stop tokens to bound response length, 2) batch similar queries where possible, 3) pin model variant with lower param count for latency-sensitive flows, 4) enable prefix KV caching for repeated contexts.

I'll attach a simple throughput-cost estimate and a sample autoscaling policy that maps traffic to Dedicated sizing if you choose that route. Laura — want me to generate the Dedicated rough estimate and share a short comparison doc?

—Rishi
